subject: Pilot commercial ask — hybrid license capex-to-opex conversion & SRE banding
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medibase.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medibase.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — commercial structure question

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile on 2k sequences and the guided onboarding plan. Two procurement items came up here that we need to resolve before the pilot PO:

1) Platform fee for the pilot environment — our finance lead is pushing to avoid a non-recurring platform fee for a 3-month pilot. Is there a path to waive or materially reduce it if we commit to a multi-quarter conversion metric?
2) Support SRE banding — we need to map actual SRE hours to your support tiers. For the pilot we expect ~40 SRE hours/month (on-call + integrations). Can you give a banded price instead of an open T&M?

Also attached is Appendix A from our RFP that lists compliance and observability must-haves (Medibase_RFP_AppendixA.pdf).

Goal: get a buyer-signed PO by 6/24. Are these negotiation levers you can run with?

Best,
Elaine Park
VP Product, Medibase Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medibase.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — commercial structure question

Hi Elaine —

Really appreciate the clear timeline. Short answers up front: yes on both, but with guardrails.

Platform fee: we can offer a reduced pilot platform fee (50% off standard) if Medibase commits to a 9-month conversion check (not a hard revenue commitment) — conversion defined as: production go-live within 3 months after pilot and usage >= 30% of pilot daily throughput for 60 consecutive days. If conversion does not occur, the discount would be invoiced pro rata.

Support SRE banding: we can offer a pilot support band that caps SRE at 50 hours/month for a fixed monthly fee. Options: 40h @ $18k/mo, 50h @ $22k/mo, with overage at $450/hr. For enterprise conversion we map SRE bands to a retainer ladder with guaranteed response SLAs.

I'll loop Ben to run the pricing math in your model and Irene to confirm procurement docs we need for the PO.

Attachment: draft term sheet (Redwood_TermSheet_v0.4.pdf) — includes pilot discount language and conversion metric template.

Can you confirm the pilot start date window (you mentioned late June)?

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medibase.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — commercial structure question

Hi Elaine, Rachel —

I ran a short model to show how the pilot discount + SRE band maps to unit economics. Key points:

- Pilot (3 months) baseline: 4x A100 equivalent hours/day peak, expected token volume ~120M tokens/month.
- Platform fee (standard): $40k one-time. Proposed pilot discounted fee: $20k (50% off) with conversion clawback if no go-live per Rachel's defn.
- Support band: 40h @ $18k/mo (pilot rate), estimated run-rate for production SRE retainer (if converted) ~ $35k/mo for 160h band.
- If Medibase wants to convert platform fee into prepay credits instead of a cash fee, we can structure a $20k credit that applies to first two months of production usage (reduces initial OPEX). That preserves your CAPEX/OPEX preference.

Tradeoffs to highlight for procurement:
- Waiving the platform fee entirely delays Redwood's onboarding cost recovery and increases implementation risk for us.
- Converting the platform fee to usage credits is the middle ground — Medibase avoids up-front non-recurring spend, Redwood captures reciprocal commitment via credits.

If those numbers look directionally OK I can produce a short commercial memo and a PO-ready redline of the term sheet.

-Ben
Senior Manager, Commercial Deals
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medibase.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -07:00

Hi all —

From a procurement and legal intake perspective, if Medibase is okay with the credit conversion approach Ben described, we need the following to move a PO to countersignature: 

- Signed NDA (if not already in place)
- PO referencing Redwood_TermSheet_v0.4 (pilot discount and conversion clause)
- SOW draft to capture scope for the 3-month pilot (deliverables + SRE banding) — I've attached an SOW draft (SOW_draft_Medibase.docx).
- SOC2 letter and minimal connectivity questionnaire (we'll provide a one-page checklist for networking).

Also: Procurement prefers pricing options enumerated in the term sheet rather than open-ended T&M. Please indicate which SRE band Medibase picks so we can lock in the rate for the PO.

I'll prepare a PO template and a short intake checklist for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Irene

Redwood Inference

Rachel / Ben / Irene,

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our procurement instincts. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- Medibase picks the credit conversion option: Redwood invoices the discounted pilot platform fee ($20k) as credit and applies it to first two production months if we convert. If we do not convert by the metric, no clawback (won't be invoiced). (We can be flexible here if Redwood needs a clawback, but our CFO prefers no retroactive billings.)
- Support band for pilot: we select the 50h @ $22k/mo option. Will expect a named SRE contact for the onboarding month.
- Pilot window: target start 29 June, duration 3 months. PO cutoff for June billing: 25 June.

I'll route the PO to procurement this week and attach the RFP Appendix. Can you send the final term sheet redline and PO template?

Tom
Director, Vendor Management — Medibase Health
